item.title: Entry Point & Annotations
item.description:
Application Entry Point link

File: org.arya.banking.admin.AryaBankingAdminServiceApplication

@SpringBootApplication(exclude = {
    DataSourceAutoConfiguration.class,
    DataSourceTransactionManagerAutoConfiguration.class,
    HibernateJpaAutoConfiguration.class
})
@ComponentScan(basePackages = {
    "org.arya.banking.admin",
    "org.arya.banking.common"
})
@EnableMongoAuditing
@EnableDiscoveryClient
public class AryaBankingAdminServiceApplication {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        SpringApplication.run(AryaBankingAdminServiceApplication.class, args);
    }
}

Annotation Breakdown link

@SpringBootApplication(exclude = ...) link

The admin-service is MongoDB-only — it has no relational database. The three excluded auto-configurations prevent Spring Boot from attempting to set up a DataSource (JDBC), a transaction manager backed by a DataSource, and Hibernate JPA. Without these exclusions, the application would fail on startup because no javax.sql.DataSource bean is present on the classpath.

item.title: Security
item.description:
Authentication Flow link

The admin-service acts as an OAuth2 Resource Server. It never issues tokens — it validates JWTs issued by Keycloak.

sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client (Postman / Service)
    participant KC as Keycloak :5433
    participant AD as Admin Service :8089

    C->>KC: POST /token (client_credentials)
    KC-->>C: JWT (realm_access.roles: ["ADMIN"])

    C->>AD: GET /api/admin/realm-roles + Bearer JWT
    AD->>AD: Validate JWT signature via JWK Set URI
    AD->>AD: Extract realm_access.roles → prefix ROLE_
    AD->>AD: @PreAuthorize → RolePermissionValidator
    AD->>AD: Lookup "query-realm" → ["ROLE_ADMIN"]
    AD->>AD: Compare with user authorities
    AD-->>C: 200 OK / 403 Forbidden
